inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: Q3 2026 10-Q weighted-average diluted shares (99M, treasury-stock method), the first full quarter after the 38.542M shares issued to BD holders on 2026-02-09. Cross-check: 98.286M basic outstanding on the 10-Q cover at 2026-11-06 plus ~0.7M dilutive awards. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the RMT issuance is already inside the count, so no further non-SBC issuance is modelled.
inputs.sbc_source: Cash-flow-statement add-back, TTM to 2026-10-03 (FY2025 10-K 54.1 - 9M-2025 40 + 9M-2026 67 = 81) plus cash taxes on net-share settlement (~15, EquityAwardTaxes KPI / 'purchases of treasury shares' line). Waters publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. Q3 2026 SBC was 22 (1.25% of revenue); FY2026E SBC ~90 + ~15 equity-award taxes = ~105 = 1.6% of FY2026E revenue, the anchor for sbc_pct_path.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate: risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST) + beta ~1.0 x ERP ~4.7% = cost of equity ~9.0%; ~10% debt weight (5.1bn debt vs ~45bn market cap) at ~4.5% after tax gives ~8.5%. Same WACC in every scenario: risk is charged once, through the scenario paths and weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: rent is already an operating expense inside EBITDA, lease liabilities (~84M legacy at FY2025, immaterial) are NOT added to net debt. One treatment, no lease_cost_pct_path.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: operating company; no bank/REIT/holdco features). First valuation of this ticker. STRUCTURAL BREAK: the Reverse Morris Trust combination with BD's Biosciences & Diagnostic Solutions business closed 2026-02-09 (38.542M shares issued, 4.0bn debt assumed), roughly doubling revenue; everything forward is built on the combined company, not the FY2021-25 standalone history. FY0 = FY2026E: base_revenue is the midpoint of raised FY2026 guidance (6,479-6,497; 9M actual 4,678 + Q4 guide 1,801-1,819), which holds only ~10.7 months of BDS. Year-1 growth therefore includes ~6pp of calendarisation (the ~5.5 weeks of BDS missing from Q1 2026, ~380M) on top of organic growth. ANCHORS: net debt = total debt 5,133 (650 current + 4,483 long-term; the Metrics CSV total_debt of 4,483 for Q3 2026 is the long-term portion only) less cash 593, at 2026-10-03; Q4 2026 cash generation is not credited, which is mildly conservative. Interest income not stripped (net debt, not net cash). last_fcf / reported_fcf are TTM to 2026-10-03 (OCF 480 - capex 189 = 291; less SBC incl. equity taxes 96 = 195) and are DEPRESSED by one-offs: 142M of transaction/integration payments, 46M restructuring payments and a 183M receivable build from BD under the TSA; they also hold only ~8 months of BDS. They are an audit trail, not the forward base: the forward flows are built from components. MARGIN BASIS: ebitda_margin_path is EBITDA before SBC, before purchased-intangibles amortisation and inventory/fixed-asset step-up, before transaction, restructuring and ERP-implementation costs. 9M-2026 on that basis: operating loss -6 + 973 purchase accounting + 64 restructuring + 176 transaction/integration + 25 ERP + 67 SBC + 168 D&A (ex purchased) = 1,467 = 31.4% of revenue; Q3 2026 alone ~34.3%; FY2026E ~33.5% with the seasonally strong Q4. da_pct_path EXCLUDES purchased-intangibles amortisation (954M in 2026, 1,078M in 2027): the RMT was tax-free, so that amortisation carries no tax basis and no cash shield; charging it would understate EBIT, crediting its shield would overstate cash. D&A ex purchased ran 3.6% of revenue in 9M-2026. Capex 150M in 9M-2026 = 3.2% of revenue (incl. ERP capitalisation). CASH TAX: adjusted rate ~16-17%; FY2023-25 cash taxes paid (183-244M) were inflated by the final 2018 Tax Reform transition instalments, which ended in 2025; path ramps 17.5% -> 19% for Pillar Two and the Singapore 5% incentive that expired 2026-03-31. WORKING CAPITAL: instrument maker with receivables + inventory > payables, so wc_capture is negative (growth consumes cash). BUYBACKS: none since Q1 2023 (58M); the flat count is a modelling convention the company is not currently funding -- cash is going to deleveraging. Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: management FY2026 organic guidance (9.1-9.7%) fading to the legacy revenue 5yr CAGR (~6%) -- NOT equity_5yr_cagr
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (62-72%) diverges far more than 30% from revenue (2-6%) and EPS (-3% to +5%) and is unusable: equity was negative in FY2019 after 2018-19 buybacks and has been rebuilding from a near-zero base; it then jumped from 2.6bn to 15.3bn in 2026 on the 12.8bn share issuance.
historical_growth.notes: All CAGRs are FY2025 endpoints on the STANDALONE pre-deal company (FY2022 and FY2020 bases) and do not describe the combined company: the BDS acquisition (closed 2026-02-09) roughly doubled revenue, lifted the share count from ~60M to ~99M and total debt from 1.4bn to 5.1bn. FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC and equity-award taxes; no interest-income strip as the company has carried net debt throughout): FY2021 547, FY2022 382, FY2023 393, FY2024 561, FY2025 471. fcf_5yr_cagr is a 4-year figure (FY2021-25) because FY2020 capex is not in the held filings. Reported-FCF 3yr CAGR is 7.4% vs 7.2% owner: SBC is small (1.7% of revenue) and not growing faster than cash flow. The forward path leans on post-deal guidance, not these figures.

base.growth_note: Year 1 = ~6pp BDS calendarisation + ~5.5% organic (down from 9%+ in 2026 as the LC replacement cycle normalises).
base.margin_note: FY2026E ~33.5%; year 1 held to 34% by TSA (~90M/yr) and residual integration cash costs; the 200M cost-synergy target (~2.9pp) lands by year 3-4; mature 37% is the legacy standalone level.

scenario_narratives.base: The combination works roughly as guided. After a 2026 in which organic growth ran 9%+ on an LC/LC-MS replacement cycle and double-digit chemistry consumables, growth normalises to ~5.5-6% (legacy Analytical & Materials Sciences mid-to-high single digit, Biosciences and Advanced Diagnostics mid single digit), fading to 3.5% by year 10; year 1 also picks up the ~5.5 weeks of BDS revenue absent from 2026. The 200M cost-synergy programme and the 120M workforce savings lift the pre-SBC EBITDA margin from ~33.5% to 37% by year 6 -- back to the standalone Waters level, not above it, because Advanced Diagnostics (26% segment margin vs 35% for the other two) stays a structurally lower-margin mix. ~70% recurring revenue keeps the path smooth; cash tax drifts up to 19% under Pillar Two.
scenario_narratives.bull: Cross-selling is real: Waters' regulated-pharma QC playbook lifts BD's flow-cytometry and microbiology consumables attach rates, clinical mass spec gains traction through BD's hospital and core-lab channel, Biosciences China (first growth in ten quarters in Q3 2026) keeps recovering, and biologics/GLP-1/PFAS testing sustain high-single-digit instrument growth. Organic growth holds 7-8% for four years. Synergies overshoot the 200M target and the TSA rolls off early, taking the margin to 39% -- above the legacy company, as Advanced Diagnostics margins converge toward the group.
scenario_narratives.bear: The largest and least familiar deal in Waters' history disappoints. The 2026 replacement cycle proves a pull-forward and pharma capex pauses; NIH and academic funding cuts land; China procurement restrictions tighten again; and in diagnostics Waters loses share to bioMerieux, Danaher (Cepheid/Beckman) and Roche in categories it has never run. Growth settles at ~3% after the calendarisation year. Synergies are absorbed by standalone-systems costs once the TSA ends and by tariff-driven material costs, so the margin stalls at 33.5%, below even the FY2026 level in years 1-2; the market pays a lower multiple (16x cap, 2.5% terminal growth) for a slower, lower-margin tools-and-diagnostics conglomerate.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 default to 20/50/30. Bear up to 20%: integration of a carve-out that roughly doubles the company into unfamiliar diagnostics categories, still dependent on a BD transition-services agreement and running an ERP replacement concurrently, is a genuine execution risk -- but not a solvency one (net debt ~2x EBITDA, ~70% recurring revenue), so it stops short of 25%+. Base 50%: the first three post-close quarters have tracked or beaten plan with guidance raised. Bull down to 30%: it needs revenue synergies, synergy overshoot and a China recovery to arrive together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Waters is a high-quality installed-base franchise (validated LC/MS methods in regulated pharma QC, ~70% recurring revenue post-deal) that has just doubled itself through a tax-free Reverse Morris Trust with BD's Biosciences & Diagnostic Solutions business. The valuation is built entirely on the combined company: FY2026 guidance as the revenue base, margins before purchase accounting and integration costs ramping on the stated synergy programme, the post-deal share count (99M) and the post-deal balance sheet (4.5bn net debt). GAAP earnings are uninformative for several years because of ~1bn/yr of purchased-intangibles amortisation that carries no cash cost and no tax shield. SBC is small (~1.6% of revenue), so the house/street band is narrow and the conclusion does not depend on SBC treatment; it depends on whether mid-single-digit growth and a 37% margin justify a price near 30x forward unlevered owner FCF.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value dominates: the result is sensitive to WACC and to the mature margin (37% base) that the synergy programme has yet to prove
Base revenue is guidance, not an audited year, and year-1 growth embeds an estimated ~380M BDS calendarisation effect

Purchase price allocation is not final; the margin basis strips ~1.25bn of 9M-2026 charges judged non-recurring or non-cash (purchase accounting, transaction, restructuring, ERP) -- if integration cash costs persist beyond 2027 the early-year flows are overstated
Cash-tax path assumes the tax-free RMT leaves no deductible step-up and that Pillar Two and the lapsed Singapore incentive add only ~1.5pp
2026 organic growth of 9%+ may be a replacement-cycle peak for instruments rather than a new run-rate
Net debt is at 2026-10-03 and the TTM FCF base is distorted by deal payments and a 183M BD receivable that should unwind
